edges.description: Defective alpha-tubulin and microtubule function impairs the microtubule-dependent nucleokinesis and translocation required for cortical neuronal migration.
Failed neuronal migration leaves neurons mispositioned, producing the smooth or abnormally folded, abnormally laminated cortex of the malformation spectrum.
Reproduces the molecular lesion class: a heterozygous missense substitution in the alpha-tubulin GTP-binding pocket that impairs heterodimer formation.
edges.limitations: The murine S140G allele is not one of the recurrent human disease alleles, and is not at the Arg402 hotspot whose dominant dynein-poisoning mechanism is best resolved in human disease.

edges.description: Reproduces abnormal laminar architecture of hippocampus and cortex with impaired neuronal migration - the tissue-level readout of this node.
edges.limitations: The mouse brain is naturally lissencephalic, so it cannot model the human gyral phenotype (agyria-pachygyria versus dysgyria versus polymicrogyria-like dysplasia) that clinically distinguishes the members of the tubulinopathy spectrum, and it lacks the outer subventricular zone and outer radial glia on which human cortical expansion depends.

edges.description: Expression of the patient allele is by itself sufficient to disrupt cortical neuronal migration in vivo, in the presence of two wild-type mouse alleles - the definition of a dominant effect.
edges.limitations: Ectopic overexpression rather than physiological expression from the endogenous locus, so the dose is not the patient dose; and the paper's own finding that dynein impairment scales with mutant expression level means the magnitude of effect is dose-sensitive by construction.

nodes.description: Heterozygous de novo missense mutations in TUBA1A alter the brain-predominant alpha-1A tubulin subunit. Disease-associated substitutions map to functionally critical regions of the protein, including the GTP-binding pocket, and impair tubulin heterodimer formation and microtubule assembly. Additional mutations disrupt the binding surfaces for microtubule-associated proteins, so that the alpha-tubulin lesion compromises microtubule structure and the docking of the regulatory and motor proteins that act on microtubules. This establishes altered alpha-tubulin function as the initiating molecular lesion of the malformation.

genetic_context.description: Disease alleles are heterozygous, almost always de novo missense substitutions; no nonsense, frameshift, or whole-gene-deletion alleles are reported, so the mechanism is not haploinsufficiency. For the recurrent Arg402 alleles the mechanism has been resolved directly: mutant alpha-tubulin is incorporated into microtubules and poisons them by populating the polymer with defective dynein-binding sites, and the degree of dynein impairment scales with mutant expression level. Comprehensive mutagenesis of all 2,683 TUBA1A coding variants further separates the allele space into classes acting on folding, chaperone engagement, and protofilament geometry, so DOMINANT_NEGATIVE describes the best-resolved recurrent alleles rather than every reported variant.

nodes.description: Impaired migration of cortical neurons disrupts the normal six-layered architecture of the neocortex, producing a coherent but broad alpha-tubulin malformation spectrum that ranges from microlissencephaly and classical lissencephaly through pachygyria and simplified gyration to polymicrogyria-like cortical dysplasia. The malformation is characteristically accompanied by dysmorphic basal ganglia, corpus callosum dysgenesis, and cerebellar and brainstem hypoplasia or dysplasia, reflecting the shared requirement for microtubule function across these developing structures.

nodes.description: Microtubules generated from TUBA1A-containing heterodimers drive the interkinetic nuclear migration of progenitors and the nucleokinesis of migrating neurons. Because TUBA1A is expressed at high levels throughout central nervous system development, the alpha-tubulin defect impairs microtubule-dependent neuronal migration. The phenotype recapitulates that of Doublecortin (DCX) and LIS1 deficiency, reflecting the functional importance of the microtubule/DCX migration machinery on which the alpha-tubulin lesion converges.

nodes.description: Not a germline model but an allele-specific perturbation: patient Arg402 alleles are expressed ectopically in the developing mouse brain. Arg402 substitutions account for about 30% of all reported TUBA1A mutations, and this experiment is what established that they act dominantly rather than by loss of one gene copy.

The founding model of the disease. An ENU mutagenesis screen recovered a heterozygous alpha-1 tubulin mutation in the GTP-binding pocket that impairs tubulin heterodimer formation, producing abnormal lamination of hippocampus and cortex with impaired neuronal migration. Its historical importance is that the direction of discovery ran mouse-to-human: the phenotypic resemblance to existing lissencephaly models is what prompted screening TUBA1A in patients with developmental brain anomalies, which found the first human cases.
